summary: Describes extensions to GMPLS signaling needed to control Optical Transport Networks defined by G.709, including pre-OTN developments. It is a companion to the GMPLS signaling documents and is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: Optical networks send data in special boxes. This memo says how to ask for a path through them using the GMPLS control system.

subtitle: How GMPLS signaling asks for and labels paths through G.709 optical transport networks.

tldr.problem: GMPLS signaling could set up paths over several kinds of links, but it had no way to describe the digital and optical layers of ITU-T G.709 Optical Transport Networks, including multiplexed and concatenated signals.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4328 adds two LSP Encoding Type values, new G-PID values, a G.709 traffic parameter block (signal type, multiplexing, virtual concatenation, multiplier) and label formats that identify the exact tributary slot of a signal.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3471, and RFC 7139 later updated it. Nodes that cannot support a request must answer with a PathErr.

today: RFC 4328 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3471, and it has itself been updated by RFC 7139. It is not marked obsolete in the unit metadata.

sections.title: G.709 Layers and the GMPLS Fit
sections.content:
This is a companion document to the GMPLS signaling documents. It covers only the technology-specific details of Optical Transport Networks (OTN) as specified in ITU-T G.709, including so-called pre-OTN developments that are not fully G.709 compliant. It deliberately does not replicate the ITU-T recommendation.

G.709 defines optical layers (OTS, OMS, OCh and reduced-functionality variants) and two digital layers, the Optical Channel Transport Unit (OTUk) and the Optical Channel Data Unit (ODUk). Only the OCh and ODUk layers are switching layers. G.709 also lets smaller ODUj signals (j = 1, 2) be multiplexed into a larger ODUk (k > j): ODU1 into ODU2, ODU1 into ODU3, ODU2 into ODU3, and ODU1 and ODU2 into ODU3.

To fit GMPLS to this, the RFC extends the "Digital Wrapper" concept of RFC 3471 into a Digital Path layer for ODUk, extends the "Lambda" concept into an Optical Path layer for OCh, and defines a label space shaped as a tree whose root is an OTUk signal and whose leaves are ODUj signals.
sections.plainLanguage: Think of shipping boxes in three sizes. Small boxes can go inside medium or large ones. The control system needs words for each box size and a way to say which slot inside a bigger box is meant.

sections.title: The Generalized Label Request
sections.content:
The Generalized Label Request has a common part and a technology-specific part. In the common part the RFC extends three fields.

LSP Encoding Type gets two new values: 12 for G.709 ODUk (Digital Path) and 13 for G.709 Optical Channel. The new values MUST be generated when the interface or tunnel supports the G.709 layer. The older Digital Wrapper and Lambda values MUST only be used for non-G.709 encodings. A transit or egress node that cannot support the requested encoding MUST send a PathErr with a "Routing problem/Unsupported Encoding" indication.

Switching Type gets no new values, because ODUk switching belongs to the TDM class and OCh switching to the Lambda class (LSC). A node that cannot support the requested value MUST send a PathErr with a "Routing problem/Switching Type" indication.

Generalized-PID (G-PID), a 16-bit field, names the client payload. New values 47 to 58 cover ODUj, OTUk(v), CBR variants, BSOT, BSNT, IP/PPP and Ethernet over GFP, ESCON, FICON and Fiber Channel. Values 32 to 35 from RFC 3471 are updated to mention G.709.
sections.plainLanguage: A request says what kind of box to use, what kind of switch handles it and what is packed inside. This memo adds new answers to those three questions for optical networks.

sections.title: G.709 Traffic Parameters
sections.content:
When the encoding type is a G.709 layer, extra traffic parameters travel with the request: Signal Type (8 bits), NMC, NVC and MT (16 bits each), plus reserved fields that SHOULD be zero when sent and MUST be ignored when received.

  • Signal Type names the elementary signal: 1, 2 and 3 for ODU1, ODU2 and ODU3 (2.5, 10 and 40 Gbps), and 6, 7 and 8 for OCh at those rates. 0 means not significant.
  • NMC (Number of Multiplexed Components) is the number of tributary slots an ODUj uses when multiplexed into an ODUk. For an ODU2 in an ODU3 it is 4; for other multiplexing cases it is 1; otherwise it MUST be 0.
  • NVC (Number of Virtual Components) is how many identical ODU signals are virtually concatenated. 0 means no concatenation, and it MUST be 0 for OCh.
  • MT (Multiplier) is the number of identical signals requested. 1 is the default and 0 is invalid; a node receiving 0 MUST send a PathErr.

Transforms apply in a strict order: first virtual concatenation (NVC), then multiplication (MT), giving the Final Signal.
sections.plainLanguage: The request is like an order form: which size box, how many slots it fills inside a bigger box, whether to chain several boxes into one long shipment, and how many copies you want.

sections.title: Labels for ODUk Signals
sections.content:
An ODUk label identifies the exact position of an ODUj signal inside an ODUk multiplexing structure. It is a 32-bit value made of three fields, t3 (6 bits), t2 (3 bits) and t1 (1 bit), with the rest reserved and set to zero.

  • t1 = 1 means an ODU1 signal.
  • t2 = 1 means an ODU2 not further subdivided; t2 from 2 to 5 selects a tributary slot used by an ODU1 inside an ODU2.
  • t3 = 1 means an ODU3 not further subdivided; t3 from 2 to 17 selects a slot used by an ODU1 inside an ODU3, and 18 to 33 selects a slot used by an ODU2 inside an ODU3.

Numbering starts at 1 because 0 marks a field as not significant. A label whose fields are all zero is invalid. An ODU2 multiplexed into an ODU3 needs 4 labels, one for each tributary slot, allocated in ascending order.

The Optical Channel layer uses a flat label space of channel (wavelength) identifiers or relative channel spacing, and its encoding follows RFC 3471.
sections.plainLanguage: The label is a street address inside the big box: which row, which shelf, which slot. A zero means that part of the address does not apply.

sections.title: Label Distribution Rules
sections.content:
The label is carried in the GENERALIZED_LABEL object (Class-Num 16, C-Type 2) as one or more 32-bit values. How many depends on the request:

  • An ODUk mapped straight into an OTUk: one label.
  • An ODUj multiplexed into an ODUk: an ordered list with one label per tributary slot (just one label when NMC is 1). The order reflects the order of the ODUj components, not the physical order of slots.
  • Virtual concatenation: an ordered list of all component labels, with the count set by NVC. This keeps concatenation inside a single component link.
  • Multiplication with the MT field: an ordered list of all labels of the composed signal. Multiplexed and concatenated cases use NVC and NMC to find how many labels belong to each set.

For signaling, G.709 traffic parameters ride in the SENDER_TSPEC and FLOWSPEC objects. A FLOWSPEC received in a Resv message SHOULD match the SENDER_TSPEC in the corresponding Path message. Intermediate and egress nodes MUST check that they can support the requested Signal Type, NMC and NVC, and otherwise send a PathErr with "Traffic Control Error/Service unsupported".
sections.plainLanguage: When you ask for several slots, the answer is a numbered list of addresses in the same order as your parts, so everyone knows which piece goes where.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The RFC walks through five cases. In the first, an ODU1, ODU2 or ODU3 maps straight into an OTU of the same order, so the downstream node returns one label such as t3=0, t2=0, t1=1 for an ODU1 in an OTU1.

In the second, one ODU1 is multiplexed into an ODU2 or ODU3 (Signal Type 1, NMC 1), and a single label such as t3=2, t2=0, t1=0 names its slot. In the third, an ODU2 multiplexed into an ODU3 (Signal Type 2, NMC 4) returns four labels, for instance t3=18, 22, 23 and 26.

The fourth is a single 40 Gbps OCh (Signal Type 8), answered with one wavelength label. The fifth requests 4 x ODU1 (Signal Type 1, NMC 1, MT 4) and returns an ordered list of four labels, the first for the first signal of the LSP, and so on.
sections.plainLanguage: Ask for one small box and you get one address. Ask for a big box that takes four slots and you get four addresses. Ask for four small boxes and you get four addresses in order.

sections.title: RSVP-TE Objects and IANA Registries
sections.content:
The G.709 traffic parameters use two new RSVP object formats: the G.709 SENDER_TSPEC object (Class 12, C-Type 5) and the G.709 FLOWSPEC object (Class 9, C-Type 5). They share the same content, and there is no Adspec associated with the G.709 SENDER_TSPEC.

IANA also tracks the extended code-point spaces. In the LSP Encoding Type registry (8-bit), values 1 to 11 come from RFC 3471 and 12 and 13 from this RFC. In the G-PID registry (16-bit), values 47 to 58 are defined here. If an MT of zero arrives, the node MUST send a PathErr with a "Traffic Control Error/Bad Tspec value" indication.
sections.plainLanguage: New numbered slots were reserved in the official lists so that every device uses the same numbers for the new optical box types.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security section is a single sentence: the document introduces no new security considerations to RFC 3473, the RSVP-TE extensions for GMPLS that it builds on. Readers worried about protecting the signaling should therefore look to that RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo adds no new locks or new dangers beyond the ones the base system already has.

fields.name: Signal Type
fields.desc: Elementary signal: ODU1 to ODU3 or OCh at 2.5, 10 or 40 Gbps.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Set to zero when sent, ignored when received.

fields.name: NMC
fields.desc: Number of tributary slots used when multiplexed.

fields.name: NVC
fields.desc: Number of virtually concatenated signals; 0 means none.

fields.name: Multiplier (MT)
fields.desc: Number of identical signals; default 1, zero is invalid.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Set to zero when sent, ignored when received.

items.label: Not significant
items.desc: Used with plain Lambda or Digital Wrapper encodings.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Set to zero when sent, ignored when received.

fields.name: t3
fields.desc: ODU3 position: 1 whole ODU3, 2 to 17 ODU1 slot, 18 to 33 ODU2 slot.

fields.name: t2
fields.desc: ODU2 position: 1 whole ODU2, 2 to 5 ODU1 slot.
